description: Pydre is a Python data-reduction package from the Ohio State University Driving Simulation Laboratory. It organizes and processes streams produced by driving simulators so researchers can extract measures from virtual or mixed-reality experiments. The JOSS description focuses on driving behaviour in dangerous or expensive scenarios, including crash-imminent events and distraction studies. The own documentation site and repository identify the software, and its licence file states Apache License 2.0. The dataset coverage, sampling rate and road scenario depend on the simulator experiment a user supplies; Pydre does not publish a fixed traffic dataset. Reduced measures can help calibrate driver-response assumptions or compare behaviours in road-safety simulation. They are also useful when simulation trials must be summarized consistently across participants. A caveat is that the package processes simulator outputs and does not establish that virtual driving reflects real-road risk. The available repository metadata did not expose a README at the usual path, so this review relied on the project documentation and JOSS article. No directly related catalogue record was established. The software was not installed or used with participant data.
